one_line: A 10 second animated New Year clip in which night-sky fireworks assemble into a glowing panda character, ending on the greeting 'Happy New Year from Elliot & friends!'.

hook.visual: Frame 0.0 is an almost empty starfield; by 1.0 s three rockets launch and two small bursts appear, and by 2.0 s large gold, white and red bursts fill the frame.
hook.on_screen_text: none in the first 7 s (the caption carries the line: 'We made an exception for fireworks past bedtime.')
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: The spectacle starts within 1 to 2 s and a central burst surrounded by smaller bursts at 3.0 s starts to read as a face (inferred), which makes viewers wait for the reveal. The caption adds a parent-voice, relatable line about breaking the bedtime rule. The 0.0 frame itself is nearly black, so the first frame is a weak static hook.

beats.observed: Near-black starfield with faint tree silhouettes appearing at the bottom by 1.0 s. No text, no characters.
Three white-blue rocket trails rise from the bottom (1.0 s), then several large fireworks in gold, white and red burst across the frame (2.0 s).

At 3.0 s a big white burst sits in the centre with four smaller gold bursts around it and two more at the top corners, arranged like a head with ears. At 4.0 s the sparks have resolved into a panda face.

A glowing panda made of firework sparks: cream face, black eye patches and ears, drawn smile, red body with a teal collar band, black arms and feet. Eyes shift side to side between frames. From 6.0 s golden spark streams fall below the feet like rocket thrust. Fireworks backdrop is gone.
Panda stays centred; a white rounded greeting appears at the top at 7.0 s and stays through the end.
beats.on_screen_text: Happy New Year from Elliot & friends!

payoff: The character reveal arrives at about 4.0 s (panda face resolves from the bursts) and the greeting text at 7.0 s.
cta: None. The on-screen text is a seasonal greeting; no follow, link or comment prompt is observed.
share_or_comment_trigger: The caption lets parents recognise their own New Year bedtime exception and answer in comments (79 comments), but sharing is weak (33 shares on 160,500 views, about 0.02 percent). The clip is mainly a pleasant watch, not a share asset.
why_it_worked: A modest breakout, not a viral one: 160,500 views is 11.2x the account median of 14,350, with a 0.51 percent like rate.
A character reveal inside 4 s on a 10 s clip makes completion and replays easy (inferred, no retention data in the file).
Seasonal timing (uploaded 2026-01-03) plus a parent-voice caption about letting kids stay up for fireworks gives a shared real-life moment.
paid_signal: no: outlier of 11.2x and like rate 0.51 percent sit in a normal organic range; boosting cannot be ruled out from the data.

solo_route.how: 1) Take a LumeBook illustration of the book hero (a stock or demo character, not a real child) and use it as the target image in an image-to-video AI tool (for example Veo, Kling or Runway). 2) Prompt for a vertical 9:16 night-sky fireworks show of about 8 s in which the bursts gradually form that character, and regenerate until the shape reads clearly by about 4 s. 3) In CapCut, add a short bold rounded greeting at about 7 s (Hebrew, with 'לומבוק' at the end) and a licensed or platform library sound. 4) Post with a parent-voice Hebrew caption about breaking a bedtime rule.
solo_route.needs: Nothing beyond AI tool credits if the character is a LumeBook demo hero or mascot. If a real customer child is the hero, written parental consent is needed. Pick the next relevant moment (Hanukkah or Gregorian New Year, Q4 2026).

lumebook_version.concept: An AI-made 9 to 10 second holiday clip where night-sky fireworks gradually assemble into a LumeBook book hero, ending on a short greeting from לומבוק. Posted with a relatable bedtime-exception caption, as a low-cost seasonal brand moment.

evidence_notes: Whisper output is only '(upbeat music)' from 0 to 2.58 s, so there is no usable speech transcript; no speech is claimed and the music is not described. All beats are observed from 10 frames at 1 s steps, so events between samples may be missed. That the panda is the character named 'Elliot' is inferred from the greeting text alone. The AI or VFX origin of the clip is inferred from the render look and cannot be verified. made_by is inferred from a branded character on the brand's own account.
